name: Ministry of Works and Development
story: Resource and infrastructure work at the Ministry of Works and Development helped establish early computer-based geographic information. The New Zealand Land Resource Inventory brought mapped information about land into a form that could be stored and analysed. Mainframe computing, resource classification and the requirements of government programmes shaped the work.

The Ministry also developed specialist computer capacity for engineering work. A. C. Shailes’s 1980 account traces its Computer Services Section to 1966 and describes the Vogel Computer Centre as a service for engineering and scientific calculations. Ministry engineers used the system to compare route and terrain alternatives for projects including the Clutha Valley and Mangaweka.
